g.text: Removing the fund documents narrows the gap but does not close it

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #52514e

g.text: Share of passages carrying each justice label, by World Bank region, before and after dropping Multilateral Climate Fund projects.

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #52514e

g.text: On distributive justice the Sub-Saharan Africa to Europe & Central Asia ratio moves only from 1.84× to 1.75×.

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #52514e

g.text: Climate justice and procedural justice shrink much more, so fund reporting was inflating those two rather than the gradient as a whole.

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #8a8983

g.text: Litigation excluded from both panels (classifiers never ran on the Sabin corpus). Documents tagged to several regions are counted in each, so rows do not partition the corpus.

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #8a8983

g.text: The ranking also survives inside a single corpus: Sub-Saharan Africa leads Europe & Central Asia on distributive justice within UN submissions (25.2% vs 12.0%) and within Policy (38.9% vs 28.7%).

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #8a8983

g.text: Source: Climate Policy Radar, PRODUCTION.PUBLISHED.PASSAGES (Snowflake), Aug 2026. Body text passages only (content_type='Text', >=20 chars), published non-principal documents.
